title_text: Should I focus on quantity or quality when working out?
content_text: Pregnancy is a period filled with new sensations and experiences as your body goes through constant changes. This transition can be very challenging, but exercising can help your body adapt! Exercise is an excellent way to care for and prepare your body for childbirth. It’s not just an essential habit for your physical well-being and health; exercise also helps relax and prepare your muscles for the pressure and weight that comes with pregnancy. We understand that finding time to exercise can sometimes be difficult, but don’t worry about that! The quality of exercise matters more than the quantity. During pregnancy, exercise doesn’t have to be long and repetitive – in fact, it shouldn’t be. You can do a few quick and simple exercises throughout the day. Ideally, you can fit them into a ten-minute break, whether it’s in the morning or before bedtime. There are numerous benefits to exercising. For example, doing multiple 5-minute exercises throughout the day can help stimulate blood circulation, uplift your mood, improve posture, prepare your body for childbirth, and tone your muscles. Consistency is key when it comes to exercise, so try to do at least two or three short exercise routines per day. Consider exercise as a time for yourself, to relax and release tension from your mind and body. Take 5 or 10 minutes to exercise and relax at the same time! Remember, the quality of exercise is more important than the amount of time you invest in it.
